heard: Most people thought NASA sent a 77-year-old into orbit for publicity. In 1998, 36 years after flying Friendship 7, sitting Senator John Glenn boarded shuttle Discovery. With President Bill Clinton watching the launch, drama struck at ignition when a drag-shoot door fell off. Critics dismissed the mission as political hype, but Discovery carried over 80 science experiments. Researchers specifically designed tests to study how spaceflight mimics the human aging process. Glenn served as a test subject, providing 17 blood and 48 urine samples during flight. He logged 134 orbits and remains the oldest person ever to reach Earth orbit. His flight delivered rigorous research on aging, even though skeptics still spread a very different story.
